items.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021
items.q: Tom Anastas who as the baritone player used to warm up Woody’s horn

ctx.x: Yes exactly. And so I said well I remember I was just kind of learning the diminished scale. So I said I better get to work on this stuff you know. And so I took my chances by

not getting a teaching gig, and I got my draft notice right away, in 1969. So but I auditioned in Indianapolis, figuring that’s close enough to Ohio, maybe I can hang in there, you know a six hour drive and whatever. And the guy in Indianapolis was very great. He had me sit in, the audition was sitting in with his big band. And he said, “You play too well, you don’t want to come and be in a fort band.” He said, “the only thing the Army can offer you is a location.” I went hmm okay. He said if you ever want to go…

innate mechanical skill. So it was just, I did a few things on my own and then started just getting back into teaching privately, and that’s kind of what I did for most of my New York career, I just taught a lot until a couple of institutions came along, Manhattan School of Music in the 80s and they were forming a jazz department and I was able to be on the ground floor of that. And then some other things that came my way, some adjunct things and some independent studies. So I was always able to kind of juggle…
